title: Demonstration of an LLO CV-QKD system over 12 km of optical fiber
authors: Christiano M. S. Nascimento, Artur A. Matoso, Gustavo C. Amaral, Guilherme P. Temporão
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) promises high rates and seamless integration with classical beams within a single optical fiber. Over the years, implementations have been performed by transmitting a local oscillator reference along with the quantum channel, opening security loopholes for eavesdroppers and limiting potential applications. Here, we report on a Gaussian CV-QKD implementation using fully independent transmitter and receiver lasers (local-oscillator sources) over a 12 km fiber spool. The system was experimentally evaluated using logical frames containing approximately $10^7$ coherent states, each composed of ten independently processed subframes of approximately $10^6$ states, and security was assessed in both asymptotic and finite-size regimes under a trusted-device model. The full-fledged classical post-processing is capable of recovering the channel parameters and extracting secret key rates of 5.11 Mbit/s in the asymptotic regime and 4.67 Mbit/s in the finite-size regime, showing good agreement with theoretical predictions. This work establishes the foundation for metropolitan fiber deployment of CV-QKD under strict security constraints.
summary: The authors report an experimental demonstration of a secure Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD) system operating over 12 km of optical fiber. By implementing a Local-Local-Oscillator (LLO) scheme, they overcome security loopholes associated with shared local oscillators. The results establish practical key rates exceeding $5 	ext{ Mbit/s}$, paving the way for metropolitan quantum networking.
main_problem: The goal was to demonstrate a secure Local-Local-Oscillator (LLO) Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD) system over a significant distance of 12 km optical fiber while mitigating security loopholes.
main_result: The experiment successfully achieved secret key rates of $5.11 	ext{ Mbit/s}$ in the asymptotic regime and $4.67 	ext{ Mbit/s}$ in the finite-size regime, validating metropolitan deployment potential.
method: The system utilized Gaussian CV-QKD with fully independent transmitter and receiver lasers, followed by complex classical post-processing including information reconciliation (using MET-LDPC codes) and privacy amplification.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an LLO CV-QKD setup implemented over a 12 km single-mode optical fiber. The security analysis was conducted under a trusted-device model, addressing the local oscillator loophole by using independent sources at both ends.
key_observables: Secret key rates ($5.11 	ext{ Mbit/s}$ asymptotic; $4.67 	ext{ Mbit/s}$ finite-size), measured average attenuation ($0.185 	ext{ dB/km}$), and excess noise ($\xi_B = 15.99 	ext{ mSNU}$).
important_parameters: Channel length of 12 km; processing large logical frames ($\approx 10^7$ states); asymptotic transmittance $	ext{T} = 0.6$.
main_assumptions: The security assessment is performed under a trusted-device model, which limits the scope of the security proof.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the experimental setup diagram for LLO CV-QKD components; Figure 2 plots the Secret Key Rate versus fiber length for both asymptotic and finite-size regimes.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, describes the sophisticated digital signal processing (DSP) routine for synchronization and parameter recovery, outlines the classical post-processing steps (reconciliation, estimation, amplification), presents the measured key rates, and discusses future work.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes quantum communication technology into practical metropolitan deployment regimes by solving critical hardware/security issues inherent in previous CV-QKD implementations.
